title: Cloud Network DNS Query Volume Spike

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `aws:route53` events matching `*` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.13.7 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:route53` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:route53` collected via Cloud networking logs via provider TA; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Cloud networking logs via provider TA
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:route53"

description: Monitors cloud networking event: dns query volume spike. This UC monitors `aws:route53` for cloud network dns query volume spike and surfaces events for SOC triage, change review, and compliance evidence.
value: DNS spikes may indicate DGA or exfiltration. Detecting cloud network dns query volume spike early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:route53.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Cloud networking logs via provider TA with the modular input for `aws:route53`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.13.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:route53.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:route53" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:route53"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.13.7_cloud_network_dns_query_7"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:route53` in `index=aws` to detect cloud network dns query volume spike. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_13_7_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Cloud networking logs via provider TA and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud network dns query volume spike so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
